'''Mizuwakasu Shrine''' (水若酢神社, ''Mizuwakasu-jinja'') is a Japanese [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima]], [[Oki District, Shimane|Oki District]], [[Shimane Prefecture]]. It is a ''[[Myojin Taisha]]''. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] [[Oki Province]] or the highest ranked shrine in the province.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Mizuwakasu Shrine {{!}} List of Geopark Sites and Treasures |url=https://www.oki-geopark.jp/en/geopark-sites-features-list/2694/ |access-date=2023-11-26 |website=Oki Islands UNESCO Global Geopark |language=en-US}}</ref> It is ranked as a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a special shrine by the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The crest of the shrine has a chrysanthemum symbol.<ref name="水若酢神社-2023a">{{Cite web |date=2023-05-28 |title=水若酢神社（Mizuwakasu Shrine） - shrine-heritager |url=https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528184043/https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |archive-date=2023-05-28 }}</ref>

It enshrines the deity Mizuwakasu-no-mikoto. This deity is linked to land development in Oki Province and sea protection.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" /><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JSMvAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu |title=Shinto shrines and festivals |date=1958 |publisher=Association of Shinto Shrines, Kokugakuin University, Institute for Japanese Culture and Classics |language=ja}}</ref>

== Overview ==

[[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja ichinotorii.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii Gate}}]]
'''Mizuwakasu Shrine''' (水若酢神社, Mizuwakasu Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]]. It is a [[Myōjin Taisha]] (Grand Shrine) of the [[Engishiki]], the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Oki Province]], and a former [[Kokuhei Chūsha]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine's crest (kamon) is "Chrysanthemum" <ref name="shrine_history"/>.

== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines the following three deities <ref name="shrine_history">Shrine history documentation.</ref>{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}:
; Main deity
:* '''Mizuwakasu no Mikoto''' (水若酢命)
; Auxiliary Deities
:* Nakagoto no Mikoto (中言命, Nakagoto Kami)
:* Suzu no Gozen (鈴御前)

=== About the Deities ===
[[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|thumb|240px|right|{{center|{{ill|Tamawakasu-no-Mikoto Shrine|ja|玉若酢命神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Okinoshima-cho, Shimane)}}{{small|The Sōja (provincial shrine) of Oki Province. The connection between "Tamawakasu no Mikoto" and "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto" is noted.}}]]
The deity's name in the [[Engishiki]] is recorded as "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine." Although Mizuwakasu no Mikoto does not appear in major texts like the [[Kojiki]] or [[Nihon Shoki]], its origins are unclear due to the loss of historical documents in fires during the Middle Ages{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The meaning of "Mizu" can be interpreted as "water" or "auspicious," and "Wakasu" is also unclear{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The connection between this shrine and the nearby Tamawakasu-no-Mikoto Shrine is also noted{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}.

The origins of the auxiliary deities Nakagoto no Mikoto and Suzu no Gozen are also unclear{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}. The traditional text "Imijuyuraki" mentions these deities{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}.

== History ==
=== Founding ===
Most of the ancient documents regarding the shrine's history were lost during the Middle Ages. According to the "Oki Chronicles" (1688), the deity appeared from the sea during the reign of Emperor Sujin and moved to its current location following the white doves{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. Another document from 1795 mentions that the deity was enshrined during the reign of Emperor Nintoku{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}.

According to local tradition, the deity moved several times before settling in its current location in Koori village during the Edo period{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=39-56}}{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=57-68}}.

The current site is thought to have been the ancient district office of the Oki Province, evidenced by the large-scale kofun (tumuli) in the area{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}.

=== Historical Summary ===
==== Ancient Period ====
In the [[Shoku Nihongi]] (842 AD), it is recorded that the shrine, along with two others, was granted official status{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}.

In the [[Engishiki]] (927 AD), the shrine is listed as "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine, Myōjin Taisha"{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. The area is identified as Kawauchi-go in the Onji District, based on the names in the [[Wamyō Ruijushō]]{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. There are no records of the shrine from the mid-Heian to the early 15th century{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}.

==== Medieval Period ====
The first medieval reference is from 1429, noting the shrine as the "Grand Shrine of Oki"{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}. It is noted as the Ichinomiya of Oki Province from 1530{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}<ref group="note">The Ichinomiya of Oki Province is sometimes identified as Yurahime Shrine, based on a note in the [[Dainihonkok Ichinomiya-ki]], but this is disputed by scholars{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}.</ref>.

In the medieval period, the Oki Province was ruled by the Oki clan, leading to conflicts and the fall of the shrine's head priests{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}.

==== Early Modern Period ====
In the Edo period, the shrine was relocated in 1676 after a flood and rebuilt at its current location in 1678{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. The main hall, built in 1795, is a designated Important Cultural Property{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}.

During the late Edo period, the shrine was involved in political movements, including the Sonnō Jōi (Revere the Emperor, Expel the Barbarians) movement{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}.

==== Modern Period ====
After the [[Meiji Restoration]], the shrine was designated as a Kokuhei Chūsha in 1871 and later registered as a Beppyo Shrine{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}.

=== Shrine ranking ===
* Senior Third rank (Engishiki) - Listed as "Mizuwakasu Myōjin."
== History ==
According to legend, the deity rose from the sea, off the shore of Igo, crossed Mt. Ōmine and entered the former Goka Village.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

The shrine might date back to the Kofun Period. This was during [[Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suijin]] or [[Emperor Nintoku]]'s reign.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

In the [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]], it was listed as a [[Myojin Taisha]] in 927.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QmdRAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu|title=Engi-shiki; Procedures of the Engi Era: Books VI-X|date=1972|publisher=Sophia University|language=en}}</ref><ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

The shrine is important in Oki Province. It guards the [[Sea of Japan]]. It appears in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'', a historical text. The ''Inshū Shicho Gakki'', from the [[Edo Period]], mentions it. The {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|sv}} names it as Mizuwakasu Myojin Oki Ichinomiya Shrine.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

The present [[Honden]] was made in [[1795]].<ref name="水若酢神社-2023a" />

It was damaged during [[Haibutsu kishaku]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y5kSAQAAMAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu|title=Business Japan|date=July 1988|publisher=Nihon Kogyo Shimbun|language=en|12=draft|12=draft}}</ref>

== Architecture ==
The shrine's style is unique. The front is ''Yuiitsu Shinmei-zukuri'', like [[Ise Grand Shrine]]. The roof is ''[[Taisha-zukuri]]'', like [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Grand Shrine]]. The pent roof is ''[[Kasuga-zukuri]]'', like [[Kasuga Grand Shrine]]. This mix is called ''Oki-zukuri''.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

== Cultural Status ==
The shrine is designated as an [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] by the Japanese government.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

== festivals ==
The grand festival is held on May 3 in odd-numbered years.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />
== Shrine Grounds ==
The shrine has been located at its current site since 1678{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. A white heron is said to have guided the deity to the present location, and a sacred pine tree called "Myōjin no Matsu" grew near the second torii gate until it died in 1971{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=39-56}}.

=== Shrine Buildings ===
[[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja honden.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|main hall (Important Cultural Property)}}]]
The main hall, built in 1795, is an example of the [[Oki-zukuri]] style, unique to the region. The building is designated as an Important Cultural Property, along with associated documents{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=91-103}}.

The worship hall, built in 1912, features a plaque inscribed with "First Shrine of Oki Province" from 1772{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=9-21}}. The gate was built in 1811{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=9-21}}.

Other examples of Oki-zukuri include the main halls of [[Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine]] and [[Ise no Mikoto Shrine]]{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=91-103}}.
<gallery>
File:Mizuwakasu-jinja suizhin-mon.jpg|Zuijin Gate
File:Mizuwakasu-jinja ninotorii.jpg|Second Torii Gate
</gallery>

=== Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli ===
[[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja kofun-1.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Mizuwakasu Shrine Kofun 1 Stone Chamber}}]]
The shrine grounds contain several kofun (tumuli) from the Kofun period, known as the Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Only two tumuli remain today:
:; Kofun 1
:: Located east of the shrine buildings. The burial facility is a horizontal stone chamber with a total length of about 11 meters, the largest in the Oki Islands. Artifacts such as iron products and beads have been found{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}<ref name="tumulus_explanation">Explanation board for Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli, set up by Okinoshima Town Education Committee.</ref>.
:; Kofun 2
:: Located behind the shrine buildings. The details are unknown{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}<ref name="tumulus_explanation" />.

== festivals ==
Major festivals at Mizuwakasu Shrine include{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=140-153}}:
* New Year's Day festival (January 1)
* Praying for Good Harvest (February 17)
* '''festival''' (May 3)
*: Known for the Sairei Furyu, a festival procession held every other year (even-numbered years). Events include the Yama-biki (Pulling the Mountain) ceremony, a procession of a decorated float called "Hōraisan," and various performances such as kagura, horseback archery, and dances. The festival is one of the "Three Great festivals of Oki" and is a designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Shimane Prefecture{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}<ref>Explanation board for Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu, set up by Okinoshima Town Education Committee.</ref>.
* Mid-year festival (June 16)
* Harvest festival (November 3)
* Gozasara festival (November 6)
* Gozairi festival (December 6)
* Year-End festival (December 31)

It was damaged during [[Haibutsu kishaku]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y5kSAQAAMAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu |title=Business Japan |date=July 1988 |publisher=Nihon Kogyo Shimbun |language=en}}</ref>

== Architecture ==
The shrine's style is unique. The front is ''Yuiitsu Shinmei-zukuri'', like [[Ise Grand Shrine]]. The roof is ''[[Taisha-zukuri]]'', like [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Grand Shrine]]. The pent roof is ''[[Kasuga-zukuri]]'', like [[:en:Kasuga Grand Shrine|Kasuga Grand Shrine]]. This mix is called ''Oki-zukuri''.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

== Cultural Status ==
The shrine is designated as an {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} by the Japanese government.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

== Festivals ==
The grand festival is held on May 3 in odd-numbered years.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

'''Mizuwakasu Shrine''' (水若酢神社, ''Mizuwakasu-jinja'') is a Japanese {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|en|Okinoshima, Shimane|qid=Q1205039|lt=Okinoshima|1=Okinoshima, Shimane}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|en|Oki District, Shimane|qid=Q735735|lt=Oki District|1=Oki District, Shimane}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|qid=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture|1=Shimane Prefecture}}. It is a ''[[:en:Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]]''. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|qid=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province|1=Oki Province}} or the highest ranked shrine in the province.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Mizuwakasu Shrine {{!}} List of Geopark Sites and Treasures |url=https://www.oki-geopark.jp/en/geopark-sites-features-list/2694/ |access-date=2023-11-26 |website=Oki Islands UNESCO Global Geopark |language=en-US}}</ref> It is ranked as a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a special shrine by the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The crest of the shrine has a chrysanthemum symbol.<ref name="水若酢神社-2023a">{{Cite web |date=2023-05-28 |title=水若酢神社（Mizuwakasu Shrine） - shrine-heritager |url=https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528184043/https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |archive-date=2023-05-28 }}</ref>

It enshrines the deity Mizuwakasu-no-mikoto. This deity is linked to land development in Oki Province and sea protection.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" /><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JSMvAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu |title=Shinto shrines and festivals |date=1958 |publisher=Association of Shinto Shrines, Kokugakuin University, Institute for Japanese Culture and Classics |language=ja}}</ref>

== History ==
According to legend, the deity rose from the sea, off the shore of Igo, crossed Mt. Ōmine and entered the former Goka Village.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

The shrine might date back to the Kofun Period. This was during {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suijin|1=Emperor Suinin}} or {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|qid=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku|1=Emperor Nintoku}}'s reign.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

In the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]], it was listed as a [[:en:Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]] in 927.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QmdRAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu |title=Engi-shiki; Procedures of the Engi Era: Books VI-X |date=1972 |publisher=Sophia University |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

The shrine is important in Oki Province. It guards the {{ill|Sea of Japan|en|Sea of Japan|qid=Q27092|lt=Sea of Japan|1=Sea of Japan}}. It appears in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'', a historical text. The ''Inshū Shicho Gakki'', from the [[:en:Edo Period|Edo Period]], mentions it. The {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|sv|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|qq=}} names it as Mizuwakasu Myojin Oki Ichinomiya Shrine.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

The present [[Honden]] was made in {{ill|1795|en|1795|qid=Q7815|lt=1795|1=1795}}.<ref name="水若酢神社-2023a" />

It was damaged during [[Haibutsu kishaku]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y5kSAQAAMAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu |title=Business Japan |date=July 1988 |publisher=Nihon Kogyo Shimbun |language=en}}</ref>

== Architecture ==
The shrine's style is unique. The front is ''Yuiitsu Shinmei-zukuri'', like [[Ise Grand Shrine]]. The roof is ''[[Taisha-zukuri]]'', like [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Grand Shrine]]. The pent roof is ''[[Kasuga-zukuri]]'', like [[:en:Kasuga Grand Shrine|Kasuga Grand Shrine]]. This mix is called ''Oki-zukuri''.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />
